title: Remote access entry (network range)
description: Expose this machine's DSH web GUI to a chosen network range (Tailscale 100.64.0.0/10 by default) on DSH 0.2.1+: only addresses inside the range are bound and peers outside it are refused, so you can reach it from a phone either with a tokenized URL or with a numeric access code; the upstream port and HTTPS follow DSH 0.2.1 automatically. Configuration has exactly one source: each Windows user's own $DSH_HOME/remote-access-config.json — the plugin never reads or writes the shared profile (cordis.patch.yml), so several users sharing one profile each keep their own port (a busy port falls back to a free one and is remembered) instead of fighting over the same one. Remote pages can also use a phone layout; Enter inserts a newline and only the send button sends; and big static assets (wallpapers and the like) are cached on the phone — where the upstream sends no cache headers this plugin supplies freshness plus a weak validator, so repeat visits stop re-transferring them (no response body is ever stored on the host). Appearance and font size can be stored in this plugin's config and projected onto remote pages only, without touching the desktop settings document; from DSH 0.2.1 work details, coding view, and performance & usage follow the desktop. The companion Android app keeps watching in the background: it raises a status-bar notification when the model asks a question while the desktop DSH window is hidden, and now also when a turn finishes — normally or with a classified failure (malformed model output, out of balance/quota, network down, rate limited, …).
